conclusions.rationale: Session identity, successful actual-start capture before overlay, own-process exclusion, stable recording/AI lifetime, restart/PID reuse and asynchronous icon references are concretely designed. Steps 1, 2, 4 and 7 plus deterministic session tests and native capture proof cover the tuple and <50 ms requirement.

source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** When a dictation starts and the frontmost application is not Handy, Handy records its identity (bundle identifier on macOS; application user model ID on Windows when available, otherwise executable path), display name, icon and process id. Application switches during the recording, processing and AI step do not change it. When Handy is frontmost, no destination is recorded.

plan_citations.excerpt: Capture when a recording actually starts, including a queued coordinator press when it drains
Capture and selection stay unchanged through recording, processing and AI except explicit badge choices.

conclusions.rationale: Most activation, final-guard, cancellation, none/off and async threading obligations are designed. However a delayed callback is prohibited from dispatch after the one-second activation deadline while configured insertion delays are preserved and the guard is after paste_delay_ms. A valid destination observed within 1 s followed by a >1 s configured paste delay would be refused by this wording, changing the configured method. Separate activation completion authorization from later guarded dispatch before READY.

source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** With "Return to the dictation's application" on (default on where supported), before insertion Handy activates the destination and waits until it is frontmost, for at most 1 second and without freezing Handy's interface, re-checks that it is still frontmost immediately before inserting (a failed re-check counts as an activation failure, without retry), then runs the configured insertion method unchanged. With the paste method "none" no application is activated. With the setting off, or without a destination, insertion targets the frontmost application as today.

plan_citations.excerpt: Include main-thread scheduling and observation latency within that deadline; a delayed callback cannot dispatch after expiry.
Its guard runs **after paste_delay_ms**, immediately before first emitted key/text or external-script launch

conclusions.rationale: Badge/icon/name and Frontmost fallback, accessible labels, none/off/unsupported suppression and settings support are assigned to Step 5 and concrete frontend/native tests. Penflow inputs are honestly deferred under the approved program decision.

source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** While the indicator is visible and "Return to the dictation's application" is on and supported, a badge next to it shows the destination icon and name, or "Frontmost app" without a destination. The badge has the accessible name "Destination: <name>". When the setting is off or unsupported, no badge is shown. With the overlay style set to none, no badge is shown and the destination behavior still applies.

plan_citations.excerpt: Icons/names or Frontmost app, badge hidden for off/unsupported/none
screen-reader badge label, toggle Tab/Space, ≤200 ms choice-to-badge measurements.

conclusions.rationale: Foreground-first ordering, non-Handy deduplication, windowed-app enumeration, selected marker, opaque versioned choices, 200 ms badge update and unchanged dismissal are specified. Freeze at insertion and stale token rejection cover the cutoff; native panel spikes and proof protect focus.

source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** Until insertion begins, clicking the badge opens a menu listing the application frontmost now first (Handy excluded), then other running applications that have windows, each with icon and name, and "Frontmost app at the end". Choosing an entry changes the destination of the current dictation only and updates the badge within 200 ms; dismissing keeps it. When insertion begins, an open menu closes and later choices are ignored. Opening and using the menu does not take keyboard focus from the user's application.

plan_citations.excerpt: At menu-open read frontmost before touching surface focus, list that non-Handy app first, then deduplicated other running applications with user windows, and finally Frontmost app at the end.
insertion entry atomically freezes selection, closes any menu and rejects late choices.

conclusions.rationale: App-closed/activation-failed/method-failed branches forbid fallback and preserve actual history status plus bounded native transcript reference. Reason visibility is ≥4 s from presentation with generation protection and capability/acknowledgement-based 010 delegation. Conditional WAV/history guarantees and style-none-before-010 staging are explicit rather than invented.

source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** If the destination is no longer running, is not frontmost within 1 second of activation, or the insertion method reports failure, no text is sent to any other application; the transcript stays in history whenever history saving succeeds as today, the indicator displays the reason (app closed, activation failed, insertion failed) for at least 4 seconds (with the overlay style none, the recovery bubble of 010 carries the reason), and the transcript is handed to the recovery features available (clipboard recovery window 007, recovery bubble 010).

plan_citations.excerpt: History guarantee is explicitly conditional as AC-005/SC-002 require: keep existing WAV-gated save, never claim history when WAV or save_entry fails.
While 010 is absent, visible-overlay failures use a dedicated reason state in the indicator for **at least 4 s measured from visible presentation**
Require a 010 consumer acknowledgement before suppressing 006's visible fallback.

conclusions.rationale: Typed status distinguishes attempted/failed/skipped/cancelled and excludes verified flags; destination, existing insertion algorithm and 007 clipboard ownership remain separate. Optional consumers receive frozen target/status/reference; 009 owns later Enter policy replacement, with existing semantics explicitly retained for now.

source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** Destination, insertion method and clipboard handling are separate settings and steps: this feature decides only which application is activated. Handy reports the outcome to the recovery features (007, 010) and to automatic Enter (009) as "insertion attempted" when the method reports success, and never reports that text was verified in a field.

plan_citations.excerpt: No `verified` success flag.
007 alone owns restoration/recovery-window policy; destination never restores or changes clipboard settings.
Provide 009 with the frozen target identity and attempted outcome

conclusions.rationale: macOS/Windows native APIs, Linux and unreadable-frontmost unsupported detection, disabled reason UI and legacy fallback are specified. A post-capture failure remains fail-closed, preserving the semantic distinction. Separate platform proof is mandatory.

source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** Support is macOS and Windows. On Linux, and wherever the frontmost application cannot be read, the setting is shown as unavailable on this system with the reason, and insertion behaves as today.

plan_citations.excerpt: Linux is explicitly unsupported; macOS/Windows become unsupported when frontmost cannot be read.
Unsupported state is `{available:false, reason}` with old insertion behavior, hidden badge and disabled toggle with localized explanation

conclusions.rationale: 006 extends the existing 008 output descriptor/domain with the exact service names, envelopes and errors. UI uses the same validation/commit path, unsupported set exit 5 is mutation-free, reads are nonmutating and real CLI/service parity tests cover CAS/no-op/concurrency.

source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** The settings CLI (008) reads and sets "Return to the dictation's application" with the same validation as the UI, including the unsupported-platform refusal. With `--json`, stdout contains only the JSON envelope.

plan_citations.excerpt: UI command uses the same SettingsMutation and pure validation/capability guard
Return exactly 008 envelopes `{ok:true,revision:N,data:{...}}` or `{ok:false,error:{code,message,details:{...}}}`
One envelope, revision and transaction implementation; unsupported refuses with no mutation, pure reads never write.

conclusions.rationale: Native/session implementation and explicit per-FR subtasks cover successful actual-start capture, stable destination state, deliberate mutation and freeze/cancellation; ownership is concrete and guarded against stale sessions.

source_citations.excerpt: **Requirement:** Capture the destination application at dictation start, excluding Handy, and keep it stable for the whole dictation unless changed from the badge.

capture before overlay display and preserve through processing/AI.

conclusions.rationale: Async activation and the injected workspace/clock/final-guard adapter are mapped to files/tests, but the one-second deadline is phrased as a dispatch expiry despite retaining configured insertion delays. source_citations.excerpt: **Requirement:** Activate the destination before insertion with a 1-second bounded wait, then delegate to the configured insertion method without changing it.

conclusions.rationale: Badge/menu/toggle file work and native non-activating surface spike cover the indicator and explicit destination selection, including main-thread focus constraints and deferred approved geometry.

conclusions.rationale: Guarded failure branches, history faults, volatile transcript retention, truthful reason metadata and optional recovery ownership are concretely mapped to Step 4/6/7 and tests. Staged absence of 010 is documented, not silently treated as durable or visible recovery.

source_citations.excerpt: **Requirement:** Never insert into another application when the destination is unavailable; preserve the transcript, report the reason and hand it to the recovery features.

plan_citations.excerpt: No destination retry/fallback on chosen-app failure
History save success/failure/not_saved matrix, reason visibility timings, outcome shape and dedup

conclusions.rationale: The method adapter remains separate, existing clipboard semantics stay with owners, outcomes are metadata-only and attempted is not field verification. Local DTO boundary and contract tests specify consumers and dedup.

source_citations.excerpt: **Requirement:** Report insertion outcomes as attempted, not verified, and keep destination, insertion method and clipboard handling separate.

plan_citations.excerpt: Introduce a thin `InsertionPort` adapter around clipboard.rs, adding an optional pre-dispatch guard, not a replacement method algorithm.
UI receives metadata only through typed `destination-changed` and `insertion-outcome`

conclusions.rationale: Capability validation is shared between native output descriptor and UI, persists only the boolean via the 008 service, and keeps unsupported reads/set refusal and reasons distinct. Step 3/5/7 provide concrete implementation and proof.

Then the badge updates within 200 ms and Comet becomes the frozen target
including ChatGPT→Comet

findings.description: The plan lets the activation deadline expire dispatch callbacks even after successful foreground observation, while preserving configured paste_delay_ms. Foreground observed at 100 ms plus a 1500 ms paste delay is a valid unchanged method under AC-002 but cannot dispatch after expiry under the plan. The timing authority is therefore contradictory.
findings.suggestion: Scope the 1 s deadline to resolve/activation/foreground authorization and its stale callbacks. Once foreground is observed within the deadline, transition to Inserting with a session/generation-bound token; preserve configured insertion delays, then perform a new cancellation/identity/frontmost guard at actual dispatch without reusing the completed activation deadline. Add a deterministic >1 s paste-delay successful-target case and a late activation callback no-dispatch case; update local contract consistently.

citations.excerpt: Include main-thread scheduling and observation latency within that deadline; a delayed callback cannot dispatch after expiry.
then runs the configured insertion method unchanged.

findings.description: Native activation/focus/Windows support and cumulative Penflow geometry/code-ir remain unproven. The plan records correct future gates and should retain these as required evidence, not convert semantic review readiness into platform or UI certification.
findings.suggestion: Keep Step 1 native failures and the one-pass program design contract as separate implementation prerequisites; attach binary-bound macOS/Windows focus traces and design authority receipts before relevant delivery.

citations.excerpt: Current `livespec penflow-contract status --project . --target web-desktop --json` is BLOCKED/certified=false
Activation restriction or focus-stealing surface blocks that platform's implementation delivery

findings.description: Direct typing and external scripts cannot provide atomic focus-and-input targeting; the plan correctly records partial-delivery and focus-race limits. These limits remain material despite successful pre-dispatch guards.
findings.suggestion: Preserve per-method native fault results and distinguish dispatch prevention from irreversible partial delivery; do not certify SC-002 as universal OS-atomic no-leak behavior from fake-adapter tests.

citations.excerpt: Native focus change between recheck and OS consumption (especially direct typing/external scripts) remains a separate residual race
Method errors after partial delivery cannot undo characters
